title: Finish the game: every mode playable
statusNote: Campaign (54 levels), Daily, Quick Play, Zen, Alien Duel, achievements, stats, music, settings.
steps: Play each mode once on a phone and on a computer
Report anything odd in the Bugs & feedback tab
feedback: Stores reject apps that crash or have broken buttons. A 10-minute play of each mode on a real phone catches most of it.
doneMessage: The game is complete. Everything from here is getting it into stores.

title: Pass the automated tests
statusNote: 107 unit tests and 28 end-to-end tests (phone and desktop) pass.
steps: Run `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` in game/ after every change
feedback: Keep tests green before every store build; a failed test is much cheaper than a rejected build.
doneMessage: Safety net in place.

title: Put everything in the ALIEN-SUDOKU folder
statusNote: game/, builds/ (one folder per platform), store-launch/, checklist/, feedback/, prompts/ in the repo; the ALIEN SUDOKU folder on your Artifacts page.
steps: Open ALIEN-SUDOKU/README.md on GitHub for the map of the folder
doneMessage: One place for everything.

title: Write the store listing text
statusNote: Name, subtitle, keywords, short and full descriptions checked against every store's limit (store-launch/listing/).
steps: Read store-launch/listing/listing.md and change anything you want in listing.json
Run `node check-listing.mjs` to re-check the limits
feedback: Keep the first two lines of the description strong: most people never tap 'more'.
Don't promise features the game doesn't have (reviewers check).
doneMessage: Copy is ready to paste into each store.

title: Fill in support email, support URL, privacy URL
statusNote: listing.json has three TODO fields only you can fill.
steps: Pick a support email you will check (a new Gmail is fine)
Decide the developer name shown in stores (e.g. Eddie G)
Use the site from 'Publish a site: privacy, support, press and play' for the support and privacy policy URLs
Put them in store-launch/listing/listing.json, or tell Claude
feedback: Google Play shows the support email publicly. Use an address made for the game, not your personal one.
The developer name should match your account's legal name or business name in each store.
doneMessage: Your contact details are set for every store.

title: Make screenshots for every store size
statusNote: 7 scenes (including the Star Cadets board) for iPhone 6.9", iPad 13", Android phone, Android 10" tablet and 1920x1080 PC (store-launch/assets/screenshots), re-made for version 1.1.0.
steps: Look through store-launch/assets/screenshots
Ask Claude for different scenes or captions if you want them
Re-make them after any visual change: `node tools/store-assets.mjs` in game/
feedback: The first 2-3 screenshots matter most; lead with gameplay, not the menu.
Captions on screenshots ('Race an alien rival') usually lift installs; they are allowed on Apple and Google.
doneMessage: Screenshots ready to upload.

title: Make store art (feature graphic, capsules, covers)
statusNote: Google feature graphic, Steam capsules and library art, itch.io cover, Microsoft and Epic art, press key art (store-launch/assets/graphics).
steps: Check each image in store-launch/assets/graphics
Steam reviews capsule art: the game name must be readable on the main capsules
feedback: Art drawn from the game's own glyphs keeps the store page honest about what the game looks like.
doneMessage: Store art ready.

title: Use the full iPad screen
statusNote: The board was limited to about 600 px wide; on iPads it now grows to fill the screen.
steps: Check the iPad screenshots in store-launch/assets/screenshots/apple-ipad-13in
feedback: Apple requires iPad screenshots for an iPad-capable app, and reviewers do test on iPad.
doneMessage: iPad layout ready for review.

title: Release version 1.1.0: the Star Cadets
statusNote: New Medium lineup (Star Cadets) and song (Cadet Mixtape) in Campaign, Daily and Quick Play; Alien Creatures move to Easy there; Zen and Duel unchanged. Version 1.1.0 (Android versionCode 2, iOS build 2).
steps: Play a Medium Quick Play puzzle to meet the cadets
Use the updated What's new text in store-launch/listing when you submit
feedback: Each store upload needs a higher build number than the last: Android versionCode and iOS build number are both 2 now.
doneMessage: Version 1.1.0 is built and published.

title: iOS project baseline is in place
statusNote: game/ios already has bundle id com.eddieg.aliensudoku, iOS 15.0 target, iPhone+iPad, scene life cycle, launch storyboard, 1024 px icon without alpha, ATT text and the encryption flag.
steps: Nothing to do: keep IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 15.0 (Apple's minimum is iOS 13).
Keep SceneDelegate: the UIScene life cycle is required when building with the iOS 27 SDK.
Keep ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false (the app only uses HTTPS through iOS).
feedback: Bundle id can't change after the first upload, so it is final now.
A layered Icon Composer icon is optional and needs a Mac with macOS Tahoe 26.4+.
doneMessage: The Xcode project already meets Apple's baseline, so the work left is accounts, privacy and ads.

title: Confirm Android SDK levels meet Play rules
statusNote: game/android/variables.gradle has targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, minSdk 24, which meets the 31 Aug 2026 rule.
steps: Keep targetSdkVersion = 36 and compileSdkVersion = 36
Keep minSdkVersion = 24 (ads SDK 25.5+ needs 24)
Re-check each August when Google raises the target
feedback: New apps and updates must target API 36 since 31 Aug 2026.
The next bump (likely API 37, Aug 2027) is not announced yet.
doneMessage: The build already meets Play's API level rule, so no SDK bump stands between you and launch.

title: Wire UMP consent and ad frequency caps in the app
statusNote: game/src/platform/ads.js runs UMP consent before ads, shows Ad privacy choices, caps interstitials and makes rewarded opt-in.
steps: Consent form shown when UMP says it is required
Ads requested only when canRequestAds is true
Interstitial every 2 games, 3+ minutes apart, never at launch
Rewarded video only after the player taps Watch video
feedback: Messages still have to be created and published in AdMob (admob-privacy-messaging).
Keep interstitials at natural breaks; never show one on app open or exit.
doneMessage: Consent and ad pacing are in place; once AdMob messages are published the flow works end to end.

title: Decide personal vs organization Play account
statusNote: No store accounts exist yet and the developer is an individual without a registered company.
time: 15 min decision (D-U-N-S would add up to ~30 days)
steps: Pick Personal unless you already have an LLC
If Organization: get a free D-U-N-S number first
Decide which Google account will own everything
Turn on 2-Step Verification on that account
feedback: Personal accounts must pass the 12-tester / 14-day closed test.
Personal accounts show your legal name and country on Play.
Switching later means transferring the app to a new account.
doneMessage: With the account type chosen you can sign up for Play Console right away.

links.label: Required info to create an account

title: Get a physical Android 10+ phone for verification
statusNote: New personal accounts must verify with the Play Console app on a real phone; we don't know if you have one.
steps: Find a non-rooted Android phone on Android 10 or newer
Install the Google Play Console app
Keep it handy for testing ads, consent and gestures too
feedback: Emulators don't count for device verification.
The same phone may verify several accounts.
doneMessage: With a phone in hand you can finish Play Console verification and test real installs.

links.label: Verify access to an Android device

title: Decide the PC price and what stays free on the web
statusNote: No PC price is set, and the full game is free on the web build, the single-file HTML and the phone apps.
steps: Pick one base price for all PC stores; $3.99 fits the $2.99-$4.99 band of Steam sudoku games.
Decide if the web version stays full and free, becomes a demo (e.g. Sector 1 + Daily), or goes offline.
Decide if you want Steam achievements (it makes Epic achievements mandatory too).
Decide if you want a free, ad-funded web version on portals at all.
Write the decisions into docs/STORE_CHECKLIST.md so every store page matches.
feedback: A complete free web game undercuts a paid PC version; sell the PC edition as complete and ad-free.
Steam launch discounts max out at 40%, then no discounts for 30 days.
Free-to-play on PC can't recoup Steam's $100 fee: there are no PC ads or purchases.
doneMessage: Price and free/paid split are settled, so every store page can be filled in the same way.

title: Verify space photo licenses and add a credits screen
statusNote: The 6 photos in game/public/space came with the prototype, sources are unknown, and the game has no credits or licenses screen.
steps: Trace each image in public/space to its source page (reverse image search).
NASA-made: public domain. ESA/Webb or ESA/Hubble: CC BY 4.0, visible credit required.
Replace any image you can't trace or license.
Add Settings > Credits: photo credits, fonts, 'made with AI assistance'.
Ship the SIL OFL license text with the fonts (e.g. a licenses/ folder in every build).
feedback: Every store agreement and Steam's content survey make you confirm you own or license all content.
Copy the ESA credit line exactly; don't use NASA/ESA logos or imply endorsement.
This applies to all PC stores, the web build and the phone apps.
doneMessage: Your content is safe to sell anywhere, removing the biggest legal risk.

title: Publish a site: privacy, support, press and play
statusNote: docs/PRIVACY.md is an unfilled template and nothing is hosted publicly yet.
steps: Fill in docs/PRIVACY.md (your name, contact email); keep 'desktop and web send no data'.
Pick a host: Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or GitHub Pages (free only for public repos).
Serve from a domain root you control (custom domain or <user>.github.io), not a sub-path.
Publish /privacy, a support email, /press and /play (web build or demo).
Add /app-ads.txt at the root once AdMob gives you the line (for the phone apps).
feedback: AdMob reads app-ads.txt from the root of the developer-website host; a github.io/Eddie-G/ path won't work.
Use a dedicated support address, not your personal email.
MS Store, Epic and portals all ask for a privacy policy URL.
doneMessage: Every store form asking for a website, privacy URL or support contact can now be answered.

title: Decide: enroll as individual or organization
statusNote: No Apple account exists yet; the choice decides the seller name and paperwork.
time: 15 min (org: +up to 7 business days for D-U-N-S)
steps: Individual: seller name on the App Store is your personal legal name.
Organization: needs a legal entity (LLC), a free D-U-N-S number, a website on its own domain and a work email on that domain.
Sole proprietors must enroll as individuals.
Pick individual unless you already have, or want, an LLC.
feedback: DBAs and trade names are not accepted for organizations.
Converting individual to organization later means contacting Apple; no timeline is promised.
As an EU 'trader' your address/P.O. box, phone and email are shown to EU users either way.
doneMessage: Choice made; you can enroll right away.

title: Enroll in the Apple Developer Program
statusNote: The owner has no Apple Developer membership yet.
steps: Make sure your Apple Account uses your legal first and last name and has two-factor authentication on.
Enroll at developer.apple.com/programs/enroll or in the Apple Developer app on iPhone.
Pay with a card in your own name.
Accept the Apple Developer Program License Agreement.
Write down your 10-character Team ID from the Membership page.
feedback: Nicknames or aliases in the name fields delay approval.
Paying with someone else's card triggers a photo ID request.
Apple gives no approval time; 2026 forum reports range from 48 hours to 3 weeks.
If the membership lapses, the app is pulled from the App Store until you renew.
doneMessage: You're in: App Store Connect, TestFlight and Mac signing are unlocked.

title: Accept agreements (no Paid Apps needed)
statusNote: No account yet; a free app with AdMob ads needs only the developer agreement.
steps: In App Store Connect > Business, accept any pending agreement updates (the DPLA changed on Oct 13, 2026).
Skip the Paid Apps Agreement, banking and tax forms: the app is free with no In-App Purchases.
Set up AdMob payments and tax info with Google instead; ad income comes from Google.
feedback: Unaccepted agreement updates block submissions; check the Business page before each submission.
You'll need the Paid Apps Agreement only for a paid Mac App Store version or IAP like 'remove ads'.
doneMessage: Agreements done; nothing else financial is needed on the Apple side for a free app.

title: Declare EU Digital Services Act trader status
statusNote: No account yet; without a status the app isn't offered in the EU.
steps: Decide: an ad-sponsored app is a listed trader factor, so declare yourself a trader.
Optionally get a P.O. box and a dedicated email/phone for public display.
In App Store Connect, enter the address (or P.O. box), phone and email.
Confirm the email and phone with the codes Apple sends.
Upload a document proving the name and address (for a P.O. box, a bill or receipt).
Certify that you follow EU law.
feedback: These details are shown publicly on the EU product page.
Declaring 'not a trader' tells EU users consumer rights don't apply; ask a lawyer if unsure.
Apple removes apps without a trader status from the EU storefronts.
doneMessage: EU storefronts are open to Alien Sudoku.

title: Check age-assurance, COPPA and image rights
statusNote: Texas SB 2420 applies since Jun 4, 2026, the art looks cute, and space photo licenses are unverified.
steps: Read Apple's age assurance Q&A and decide with a lawyer whether you must check age ranges (Texas, Utah, Louisiana).
Keep all marketing aimed at teens and adults; never say 'for kids'.
If many players may be under 13, ask Claude to add a neutral age question and child-directed ad requests.
Find the source and license of each space photo in game/public/space and add credits in About.
feedback: App Review doesn't test the state laws today, but liability is yours.
ESA images are often CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO: credit and share-alike apply.
App Store Connect asks you to confirm rights to third-party content.
doneMessage: Legal loose ends are known and the content rights answer is honest.

title: Create Play Console account and verify identity
statusNote: No Play Console account exists yet.
steps: Go to play.google.com/console/signup and choose Personal
Enter developer name (e.g. Eddie G) and public developer email
Create or pick the Google payments profile (legal name, address)
Verify contact email and phone with the one-time codes
Pay the $25 fee with a card in your name
Upload your government ID when asked
Verify with the Play Console app on your Android phone
feedback: Legal name must match your ID and payments profile exactly.
Keep the contact email and phone working for the account's lifetime.
The fee is not refunded if verification fails on bad info.
doneMessage: Your developer account is live, so you can create the app and claim com.eddieg.aliensudoku.

title: Declare EU trader status (due 1 Feb 2027)
statusNote: Required of every Play account from Nov 2026 (reported); no account exists yet.
cost: Optional PO box / second phone line
time: 15 min (+ setting up a business address if wanted)
steps: Open Play Console > Account details > Declare status
Ad-funded app in the EU/UK: answer Trader
Enter and verify a public phone number and address
Or exclude EEA/UK countries if you won't disclose them
feedback: Trader details show to EU/UK users from 1 Mar 2027 (reported).
Choosing non-trader just to hide details risks suspension.
Could not verify on a Google page; follow the Console banner.
doneMessage: Trader status is settled, so updates won't be blocked and EU users can keep installing.

title: Create the app and claim the package name
statusNote: No Play Console app exists; com.eddieg.aliensudoku is not yet registered.
steps: Play Console > Create app
Name: Alien Sudoku; language English (US)
Type: Game; Free
Enter package name com.eddieg.aliensudoku if asked
Accept the policy and export law declarations
Check Android developer verification shows Registered
feedback: Creating the app auto-registers the package for developer verification.
A free app can never become paid later.
doneMessage: The package name is yours; you can now fill in App content while builds get sorted out.

title: Create and verify the AdMob account
statusNote: No AdMob account exists; the app uses Google's test ids.
time: 20 min + up to 24 h review (rarely 2 weeks)
steps: Sign in at admob.google.com with your long-term Google account
Choose Individual account type
Accept the AdMob terms
Enter payment details so the account can be verified
Wait for the approval email
feedback: One AdMob account per person; close any old one first.
Account type can't be changed later.
doneMessage: AdMob is approved, so you can create the real app id and ad units.

title: Add the Android app and three ad units in AdMob
statusNote: game/android/.../strings.xml and ads.js still use Google test ids.
steps: Apps > Add app > Android > Not listed on a store yet
Copy the app id (ca-app-pub-...~...)
Create units: Banner (adaptive), Interstitial, Rewarded
Rewarded: amount 1, item hint
Send Claude the app id, 3 unit ids and your pub- id
feedback: Ad unit ids aren't secret, but keep test and live builds separate.
New units can take up to an hour to serve.
doneMessage: Real ids are ready; Claude can wire them into the production build.

title: Publish GDPR and US state consent messages
statusNote: The app calls UMP, but no messages exist until you create them in AdMob.
steps: AdMob > Privacy & messaging > European regulations: create message
Add your privacy policy URL; choose Consent + Manage options
Pick the Android app; publish
Create a US states regulations message; publish
Test with UMP debug geography on your phone
feedback: Without a published GDPR message, EEA/UK users get no consent form and fewer ads.
The in-app Ad privacy choices button reopens these forms.
doneMessage: Consent is compliant in the EU, UK and regulated US states.

title: Set max ad content rating to PG or G
statusNote: The app already requests PG-max ads in code; also set it in the AdMob console so it applies everywhere.
steps: AdMob > Blocking controls > Ad content rating
Choose PG (or G for maximum safety) for the app
Optionally block sensitive categories (dating, gambling)
feedback: Play requires ads to suit the app's content rating (likely 3+/7+).
G/PG also lowers risk given the cute art.
doneMessage: Ads will match a family-friendly rating, protecting your listing and target audience answers.

title: Prepare legal name, bank account and tax ID
statusNote: No store accounts or payout details exist yet; every PC store asks for the same data.
cost: $0 (an EIN is free from the IRS)
steps: Choose: sell as an individual (SSN) or sole proprietor/LLC (EIN).
Optional: get a free EIN at irs.gov so your SSN isn't on store tax forms.
Have a bank account in exactly your legal name (or the LLC's).
Get a business address and phone you're OK showing EU buyers (DSA trader info).
Keep W-9 details ready; each store runs its own tax interview.
feedback: Steam rejects aliases and DBAs: legal name, tax name and bank name must match.
A newly issued EIN can take up to 30 days to validate in Steam's tax check.
A PO box or virtual office keeps your home address off EU store pages.
doneMessage: You have everything every store's payout and tax forms will ask for.

title: Join Steamworks and pay the $100 Steam Direct fee
statusNote: No Steamworks account yet; the 21-day release wait starts only when the fee is paid.
steps: Use a Steam account with Steam Guard mobile authenticator on.
Go to partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect; enter your legal name and address.
Sign the Steam distribution agreement.
Pay the $100 Steam Direct fee to get the App ID.
Add a phone number: SMS codes are needed to set builds live after release.
feedback: Pay early: the 21-day wait (30 in an older doc revision) counts from payment.
Only an admin of the partner account can pay the fee.
Demos are separate App IDs tied to this game; no extra fee was found in the docs.
doneMessage: You have an App ID; build the store page and depots while verification runs.

title: Finish Steam tax interview, bank and identity checks
statusNote: Needs the Steamworks account first.
steps: Do the tax interview (TaxIdentity by Lilaham) in one sitting; W-9 data for US.
Enter bank routing number, account number and bank address.
Answer any document requests from Valve quickly.
Watch the Steamworks dashboard until it shows verified.
feedback: The interview can't be saved halfway; have your SSN or EIN at hand.
Name mismatches between tax, bank and legal name cause most delays.
doneMessage: Valve can pay you, and release becomes possible once the wait and reviews are done.

title: Create an itch.io account and set up payouts
statusNote: No itch.io account yet.
steps: Sign up at itch.io and verify your email.
Payment settings: pick 'Collected by itch.io, paid later' (handles VAT) or 'Direct to you'.
Complete the tax interview (W-9) to avoid 30% withholding.
Set your revenue share (default 10% to itch; any 0-100%).
feedback: Payment-processor fees (about 2.9% + $0.30) come on top of itch's share.
Payouts can be held for review; don't plan cash flow around launch day.
doneMessage: You can create the itch.io page and take payments.

title: Register a free Microsoft Store individual account
statusNote: No Partner Center account yet.
cost: Free for individuals ($99 one-time for companies)
steps: Sign in to Partner Center with a personal Microsoft account.
Choose Individual developer; verify with government ID and a selfie.
Fill in the tax profile (W-9) and payout account.
Apps and games > New product > MSIX or PWA app; reserve 'Alien Sudoku'.
Copy Package/Identity/Name, Publisher (CN=...) and display name from Product identity.
feedback: Choose MSIX, not EXE/MSI: Microsoft signs MSIX for free and sells it for you.
Use the same publisher name ('Eddie G') as on your other stores.
doneMessage: The name is reserved and you have the identity values the MSIX build needs.

title: Optional: open an Epic Developer Portal org, pay $100
statusNote: No Epic account; lower priority than Steam, itch and Microsoft Store.
steps: Create an Epic account (18+) and an organization of type Individual.
Accept the Epic Games Store Distribution Agreement.
Complete trader verification, the tax interview (W-9) and Hyperwallet payout.
Pay the $100 submission fee for the product.
feedback: You keep 100% of the first $1M net per product per year, then 88%.
Epic First Run (6 months at 100%) needs PC exclusivity; skip it.
Skip Epic for now if time is short; small puzzle games get little traffic there.
doneMessage: You can create the Epic product page and upload builds.

title: Build the playable web version
statusNote: builds/web/AlienSudoku.html plays offline in any browser; also published in the ALIEN SUDOKU folder on claude.ai.
steps: Open builds/web/AlienSudoku.html in a browser to play
Rebuild with `node tools/package-artifact.mjs` in game/
doneMessage: Anyone can play it in a browser.

title: Build Windows, Linux and macOS apps
statusNote: Built Nov 17 from the current game: Windows installer + portable, Linux AppImage + deb, macOS Intel + Apple Silicon zips (unsigned). About 100 MB each, so not in git; see builds/<platform>/README.md.
steps: Ask Claude to send you the files, or rebuild them with the commands in each builds/<platform>/README.md
feedback: Unsigned Windows installers show a SmartScreen warning; unsigned Mac apps won't open without right-click > Open. Fine for testing, not for stores (see the signing tasks).
doneMessage: Desktop builds exist for every PC store.

title: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the iOS app
statusNote: Done: game/ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (UserDefaults, reason CA92.1) added to the app target.
steps: Create game/ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy.
Declare NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults with reason CA92.1.
Set NSPrivacyTracking false and leave tracking domains and collected data empty (Google's SDK ships its own).
Add the file to the App target's Resources in project.pbxproj.
After the first archive, check Xcode's privacy report and the upload email.
feedback: The file name must be exactly PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy.
Capacitor and Cordova are on Apple's SDK list; Capacitor 8 ships its own manifests.
Re-check when adding any plugin that touches files, disk space, boot time or keyboards.
doneMessage: The biggest upload blocker is gone.

title: Add privacy policy and Report-an-ad links in app
statusNote: Done: Settings has "Privacy policy" and, on phones, "Report an ad" (guideline 2.5.18).
steps: Add a 'Privacy policy' button in Settings > Privacy & data that opens the hosted policy.
Add 'Report an inappropriate ad' that opens an email or form (include time and screen).
Show both only where ads exist, or always for the policy.
Mention both in the App Review notes.
feedback: Guideline 2.5.18 now requires a way to report inappropriate or age-inappropriate ads.
Missing in-app privacy links are a common 5.1.1 rejection.
doneMessage: Two likely rejection reasons are fixed.

title: Switch to real AdMob ids, SKAdNetworks, ad rating
statusNote: The app now caps ads at PG (maxAdContentRating). Still to do: real AdMob ids and Google's full SKAdNetwork list.
time: 1 hour after AdMob is set up
steps: You: create the iOS app and banner, interstitial and rewarded units in AdMob; publish the GDPR and IDFA explainer messages.
You: set AdMob blocking controls to max ad content rating G or PG and block sensitive categories.
Claude: run tools/set-admob-ids.mjs and set the VITE_ADMOB_IOS_* values or secrets.
Claude: add Google's full SKAdNetwork list to Info.plist.
Claude: pass maxAdContentRating 'ParentalGuidance' (or 'General') to AdMob.initialize().
feedback: Ads must fit the 9+ age rating (2.5.18).
Register your phone as a test device; never tap your own live ads.
developers.google.com was unreachable here; fetch the SKAdNetwork list where it is reachable.
doneMessage: Builds now earn money and show age-appropriate ads.

title: Get a Mac build path working
statusNote: There is no Mac, and GitHub Actions jobs fail in ~2 seconds without a runner on this account.
steps: First try: fix GitHub billing/spending limit or account flag, then re-run the workflow (the repo is public).
Fallback: Codemagic personal account (500 free macOS minutes/month) with a codemagic.yaml.
Or rent a Mac (MacinCloud pay-as-you-go) or borrow one for a manual archive.
Xcode Cloud only after one Mac session, since Apple requires Xcode for the first workflow.
feedback: macos-latest runs macOS 26 with Xcode 26.6, which meets today's rule.
From April 2027 builds need Xcode 27 (GitHub label xcode-27 is in preview).
Pricing for Codemagic, MacinCloud and GitHub was not re-verified here.
doneMessage: You can produce signed iOS builds without owning a Mac.

title: Register bundle id com.eddieg.aliensudoku
statusNote: Needs the developer account; the id already matches the Xcode project.
steps: developer.apple.com > Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles > Identifiers > +.
Choose App IDs > App, explicit id com.eddieg.aliensudoku, description Alien Sudoku.
Leave all capabilities off (no push, no Game Center).
feedback: The id must match Xcode exactly and is permanent after the first upload.
doneMessage: The bundle id now appears in App Store Connect's New App form.

title: Create the app in App Store Connect
statusNote: No App Store Connect account or app record exists yet.
steps: App Store Connect > Apps > + > New App.
Platform iOS, name Alien Sudoku, language English (U.S.).
Bundle id com.eddieg.aliensudoku, SKU alien-sudoku-ios, Full Access.
Create it now to reserve the name.
feedback: Names are 2-30 characters and must be unique on the App Store.
SKU can't be changed later.
doneMessage: The app exists in App Store Connect; builds can be uploaded to it.

title: Create an Admin App Store Connect API key
statusNote: Repo docs say 'App Manager', but cloud signing via xcodebuild with an API key only works with an Admin key.
steps: Users and Access > Integrations > App Store Connect API (request access first if asked).
Team Keys > + > name 'CI', role Admin.
Download the .p8 (only once) and note the Key ID and Issuer ID.
Store it in a password manager, never in git.
feedback: With an App Manager key the build fails with 'Cloud signing permission error'.
Revoke the key right away if it leaks.
doneMessage: CI can now sign and upload builds for you.

links.label: Forum: Admin needed for cloud signing

title: Add Apple secrets and fix CI signing docs
statusNote: The iOS job exists but GitHub Actions doesn't start, and docs name the wrong key role.
steps: You: add APPLE_TEAM_ID, ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID and ASC_KEY_P8_BASE64 as secrets.
Claude: change 'App Manager' to 'Admin' in docs/STORE_CHECKLIST.md and the iOS prompt.
Claude: pin runs-on to macos-26 now and plan xcode-27 before April 2027.
Claude: if Codemagic is chosen, add codemagic.yaml with the same steps.
feedback: Build numbers come from the run number; never reuse one.
If manual signing is preferred, store a distribution .p12 and profile instead.
doneMessage: Every push can produce a TestFlight build.

title: Archive and upload the first build
statusNote: Needs a working Mac/CI path, the privacy manifest and the app record.
steps: Run the iOS job (or archive on a Mac: npm ci, npm run cap:sync, Xcode > Product > Archive).
Upload to App Store Connect.
Read the processing email for ITMS warnings (privacy, SDK signatures).
Confirm the build shows in TestFlight with no 'Missing Compliance'.
feedback: Uploads must use Xcode 26+ now and Xcode 27 from April 2027.
Fix every ITMS warning before submitting for review.
doneMessage: Your first iOS build is in App Store Connect.

title: Sign and notarize the Mac desktop build
statusNote: desktop/package.json has identity null, there's no Developer ID cert, and signing needs macOS.

title: Create and back up the upload key

Decide if Age Signals API is needed (likely not for v1)
feedback: Never use age signal data for ads or analytics.
Re-check before adding purchases or accounts.
doneMessage: You know your US age-law obligations before going public.

title: Apply for production access
statusNote: Unlocks only after the closed test completes.
steps: Dashboard > Apply for production
Describe recruitment, engagement and feedback
Explain what you changed and why it's ready
Submit and wait for the email
feedback: Vague answers get rejected; be specific.
If rejected, fix what Google names and reapply.
doneMessage: Production (and open testing) is unlocked for your account.

title: Release to production with real ads
statusNote: Needs production access and a build with real AdMob ids.
steps: Upload the AAB with real ids and a higher versionCode
Choose countries (consider trader status for EEA/UK)
Use a staged rollout, e.g. 20% then 100%
Optionally turn on Managed publishing
Submit for review
feedback: Make sure the store listing matches the build.
Fix any pre-launch report crashes before submitting.
doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is live on Google Play!

title: Submit the Steam page for review, go Coming Soon
statusNote: No store page yet.
time: 3-5 business days review; then 2+ weeks live
steps: Complete the store page items in the Steamworks release checklist.
Submit for review at least 7 business days before you want it public.
Once approved, publish as Coming Soon with a date.
Keep it public at least 2 weeks before release.
feedback: Within 14 days of release the date is locked unless Valve changes it.
Common fixes: text in capsules, features the build lacks, non-gameplay screenshots.
doneMessage: The page is public and collecting wishlists.

title: Submit the build for Steam review
statusNote: No build uploaded yet.
steps: Mark the release-candidate build ready in the release checklist.
Submit for build review.
If it fails, fix, upload and resubmit.
feedback: Valve checks it launches on every listed OS and that listed features exist; it is not QA.
doneMessage: The build is approved; you can release once the wait and Coming Soon time are done.

title: Request a Steam Deck compatibility review
statusNote: Needs a passed build review; no controller support yet.
steps: After build review passes, open Technical Tools > Steam Hardware Compatibility Review.
Request the review.
Read the result in the week before it goes public; fix and re-request if needed.
feedback: A missing badge doesn't block release.
Without gamepad support expect Playable or Unsupported.
doneMessage: Deck and Steam Machine owners can see how well the game runs.

title: Submit to Microsoft Store certification
statusNote: No package or listing yet.
time: Up to 3 business days (first app can be longer)
steps: Upload the .appx/.msix under Packages.
Check every section is complete and submit.
Choose manual publish so you control the release moment.
feedback: Stuck past 3 business days? Open a free Partner Center support ticket.
Content, screenshots and age rating must match.
doneMessage: Certification passed; publish whenever you're ready.

title: Optional: upload with BuildPatchTool, submit to Epic
statusNote: No Epic organization or product yet.

steps: Get the BuildPatchTool client ID and secret from Product Settings.
Upload out/win-unpacked with -mode=UploadBinary; app launch 'Alien Sudoku.exe'.
Set the binary active and add the Windows platform in Artifacts.
Submit the offer and binary for review.
feedback: The build must match the store description.
Use the newest BuildPatchTool version Epic's docs list.
doneMessage: Epic has your build; release follows approval.

title: Release and link the app in AdMob
statusNote: Waits for approval.
time: 30 min + up to ~7 days app-ads.txt check
steps: Press Release This Version.
In AdMob, link the iOS app to its App Store listing.
Check that app-ads.txt shows as verified.
Set promotional text and reply to early reviews.
feedback: Ad fill can be limited until AdMob verifies the app.
If the app stays 'Processing' for hours, check the accessibility section.
doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is live on the App Store and earning from ads.

title: Prepare for Jan-Apr 2027 Apple deadlines
statusNote: CI uses Xcode 26.6; no Duo screenshots; new age questions not answered.
steps: By Jan 12, 2027: answer Shared Location and Dating (No/No) in the age rating.
Before April 2027: build with Xcode 27 / iOS 27 SDK (CI label xcode-27 or macOS 27).
Test on iPhone Duo in Device Hub and add Duo screenshots.
Renew membership and keep TestFlight builds fresh (90 days).
feedback: Updates built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later need iPhone Duo screenshots from April 2027.
Watch developer.apple.com/news for new requirements.
doneMessage: Updates keep flowing after Apple's 2027 changes.

title: Decide later on a Mac App Store version
statusNote: PC price is undecided and no MAS build target exists.
steps: Wait until the iOS launch and desktop price are settled.
If yes: new macOS app record with its own bundle id (e.g., com.eddieg.aliensudoku.mac).
Claude adds an electron-builder mas target with sandbox entitlements.
Sign the Paid Apps Agreement, tax and banking; join the Small Business Program.
Mac screenshots at 2880x1800 (16:10).
feedback: Mac App Store apps must be sandboxed and update only through the store (2.4.5).
Using the iOS bundle id would make it a free universal purchase.
doneMessage: You've made a deliberate call on the Mac App Store.

title: Link the AdMob app to the live Play listing
statusNote: AdMob can only link after the app is public on Play.
steps: AdMob > Apps > Alien Sudoku > App settings
Add app store details; search the Play listing
Wait for the app readiness review email
feedback: Ads are limited until the review and app-ads.txt pass.
Closed-test apps can't be found in store search.
doneMessage: AdMob has verified the app, so ads can serve fully.

title: Publish and verify app-ads.txt
statusNote: No developer website or app-ads.txt exists yet.
steps: Copy the line from AdMob > Apps > app-ads.txt
google.com, pub-XXXX, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0
Serve it at https://<website-host>/app-ads.txt
Make sure the Play listing website is that same host
AdMob > app-ads.txt tab > Check for updates
feedback: Must be at the root of the host, not a sub-folder.
Status can take 24 hours or more to update.
doneMessage: Advertisers can verify your inventory, which lifts limited serving.

title: Add tax info, bank details and verify the PIN
statusNote: No AdMob payments profile or tax info yet.
time: 30 min + ~3 weeks for the PIN letter
steps: AdMob > Payments > Manage settings
Add US tax info (W-9, individual)
Add a bank account for EFT
Enter the mailed PIN when it arrives (within 4 months)
feedback: Payments go out around the 21st once over $100.
Tax info must be in by the 20th to be paid that month.
doneMessage: Your ad earnings can be paid out each month.

title: Monitor vitals, policy and 2027 deadlines
statusNote: Nothing is live yet to monitor.
steps: Check Android vitals: crashes, ANRs, memory
Check Play policy inbox and AdMob policy center
Reply to reviews
Calendar: 1 Feb 2027 trader + 16 KB; Feb 2027 memory/DEX
feedback: Crash rate above 1.09% hurts visibility.
Respond to policy emails before the deadline.
doneMessage: You'll catch problems before they cost installs or ad revenue.

title: Plan the 2027 ads SDK and target API upgrade
statusNote: @capacitor-community/admob 8.3 uses legacy ads SDK 25.4.x, deprecated 30 Jun 2027.
steps: Track the plugin's Next-Gen SDK support
Upgrade before 30 Jun 2027 (sunset 30 Jun 2028)
Bump targetSdk when Play announces the 2027 level
Re-run consent and ad tests after upgrading
feedback: After sunset, ads may stop serving entirely.
Android 17 target removes the large-screen opt-out.
doneMessage: Ads and API levels stay current, so revenue doesn't stop in 2028.

title: Optional: publish on Samsung Galaxy Store
statusNote: No Samsung seller account; optional after Play launch.

Request commercial seller status (needed even for free apps)
Download the Play-signed universal APK from App bundle explorer
Import the listing from Play; upload the APK
Or register your own signing key in Play's developer verification page
feedback: Galaxy Store enforces Android developer verification.
AdMob works on Samsung phones (they have Google Play services).
doneMessage: Samsung phone owners can find the game in their default store too.

title: Skip Amazon Appstore and Huawei AppGallery for now
statusNote: Amazon closed its Android phone store on 20 Aug 2025; Huawei phones lack Google ads services.
steps: Note Amazon only serves Fire tablets/TV now
Note HUAWEI Ads doesn't accept individuals
Revisit only if you add another ad network
feedback: AdMob depends on Google Play services, missing on Fire and new Huawei devices.
doneMessage: You can focus on Google Play, where the audience and ad revenue are.

title: Publish the itch.io page
statusNote: No itch project yet.
steps: Switch visibility from Draft/Restricted to Public.
Post a launch devlog with a link to the Steam page.
Push updates with butler; post a devlog for each.
feedback: itch is a good soft launch: fix early feedback before Steam.
doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is live and playable on itch.io.

title: Optional: enter Steam Next Fest with a demo
statusNote: Feb 2027 fest (Feb 22-Mar 1): register by Jan 10, 2027; next one June 14-21, 2027.
steps: Build a demo (e.g. Sector 1 + Daily) as a separate demo app; pass its build review.
With the base game page public, register before the deadline.
Submit demo + page for review by Valve's date (Jan 18 for press preview).
Release the full game after the fest ends.
feedback: A game gets only one Next Fest; enter when the demo is polished.
February is tight from today; June 2027 is the realistic fest.
doneMessage: Your demo is in front of fest players and wishlists can grow.

title: Release on Steam
statusNote: Nothing on Steam yet.
steps: Confirm: 21 days since paying, 2+ weeks Coming Soon, build reviewed, account verified.
Set the reviewed build live on the default branch.
Press Release in Steamworks at your chosen time.
Post a launch announcement and answer early reviews.

Avoid launching in the middle of a big seasonal sale.
doneMessage: Alien Sudoku is on Steam. Watch reviews and patch quickly in week one.

title: Publish on the Microsoft Store
statusNote: Not submitted yet.

Check the live listing, rating and price.
Ship updates as new MSIX submissions with higher versions.

doneMessage: Windows users can buy the game straight from the Microsoft Store.

statusNote: Not submitted yet.

statusNote: Starts after release.
steps: Read reviews and bug reports daily for 2 weeks; patch via beta then default.
Re-request the Deck review after input fixes.
Join seasonal sales once 30 days have passed since launch.
Post an update event with every patch.
feedback: Discounts need a 30-day cooldown, except seasonal sales.
Reply calmly to reviews about AI or price; point to the disclosure.
doneMessage: The game keeps improving and shows up in sales.

title: Submit Alien Sudoku to GOG after the Steam launch
statusNote: Nothing submitted; GOG only reviews near-final or released games.
time: 30 min form; reply in weeks or never
steps: Wait until it's out on Steam with some reviews.
Fill in the ~15-question form at gog.com/submit-your-game.
Link the Steam page, trailer and a build or key.
State DRM-free, offline play, Windows build ready; be open about AI-assisted art.
feedback: GOG is highly curated; odds for a small sudoku game are low.
GOG's audience pushed back hard on generative AI in 2026.
doneMessage: Your submission is in; carry on and treat a GOG yes as a bonus.

title: If accepted: deliver GOG builds and assets
statusNote: Blocked until GOG accepts the game and sends a contract.
steps: Sign the distribution agreement; check the revenue share (commonly 70/30).
Upload win-unpacked (and Linux/Mac if wanted) via Build Creator or Pipeline Builder.
Confirm it runs offline without GOG Galaxy (DRM-free).
Deliver key art, logo, layered PSD, screenshots and a trailer with GOG's end slate.
Send the release candidate at least 3-5 days before launch.
feedback: GOG builds the offline installers on its servers.
The Galaxy SDK (achievements, cloud) is optional.
doneMessage: GOG has everything it needs to sell the game DRM-free.

title: Optional: try a CrazyGames Basic Launch
statusNote: The web build fits the limits (2.4 MB) but there's no portal account and a free web version may clash with PC pricing.
steps: Confirm a free web version fits your PC plan.
Create a CrazyGames developer account; upload the web zip (no SDK for Basic Launch).
Remove links to app stores, Steam or other web versions from that build.
Basic Launch runs 7-21 days (needs 500+ plays); watch the stats.
For Full Launch add the CrazyGames SDK (ads, account-linked saves).
feedback: No app-store links or cross-promotion in game; community links only in the menu.
Content must fit PEGI 12; the gnarly aliens are fine.
The revenue split isn't published; ask before SDK work.
doneMessage: You'll know if web players like the game before investing in portal ads.

title: Optional: add a portal ads adapter (CrazyGames/Poki)
statusNote: src/platform/ads.js only drives AdMob on phones; web and desktop have no ads.
steps: Add a portal adapter behind a build flag.
Map interstitial to midgame/commercial break, rewarded to rewarded break.
Mute music and pause input during ads; send gameplay start/stop events.
Use the portal's save/data API if required; keep PC and itch ad-free.
feedback: Portals allow only their own SDK ads.
Reuse the existing 'between games' and 'extra hint/second chance' moments.
doneMessage: A portal build can earn ad revenue without touching the PC version.

title: Optional: apply to Poki (web-exclusive deal)
statusNote: Not applied; Poki's program is closed beta and prefers web exclusivity.

steps: Read Poki's deal types; Web Exclusive is the default.
If you accept, plan to remove the web build from itch and your site.
Apply through Poki's submission form with a playable link.
If accepted, integrate the Poki SDK.
feedback: Exclusivity covers only the open web; Steam and mobile stay fine.
Term length is reported as 5 or 7 years; read the contract.
doneMessage: Poki reviews the game; a deal could fund the web version.
